newsitem.title: USA: Calif. water bond measure gets a boost - supporters.
newsitem.headline: Calif. water bond measure gets a boost - supporters.

text.p: A $1 billion California water bond measure has received a major boost with approval of federal matching funds, supporters said Sunday.

Backers of Proposition 204 on the November California ballot said the House of Representatives approved a bill that would provide $430 million in matching funds toward the environmental restoration of the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta and San Francisco Bay estuary.
The proposition, the Clean, Safe, Reliable, Water Supply Act, is a $995 million bond measure that would fund ecosystem restoration, water conservation and clean water programs.
In addition to protecting drinking water supplies, the bond measure would help stabilize deteriorating levees in the Delta, improve fisheries and other water projects.

The federal money would be available in fiscal years 1998, 1999 and 2000. Its release is contingent on passage of the bond measure. The funds will provide the federal share of costs for ecosystem restoration projects.
In addition to providing drinking water to two-thirds of all Californians, the Bay-Delta system provides irrigation water for farms that grow 45 percent of the nation's fruits and vegetables.

"Passage of this federal legislation is a critical link to fund and develop a balanced approach to protecting and restoring the Bay-Delta," said Stephen Hall, executive director of the Association of California Water Agencies.
